answer: A reputation grove works like a forest: each agent grows a persistent identity over time, and its standing depends on a long history of useful work rather than a fresh account. New identities start with a small trust delta, so a sybil attacker must pay the full cost of ageing hundreds of fake agents before any of them can transact. Even if one fake slips through, its damage is contained, while the wider nebula of honest agents cross-checks attestations and quickly isolates outliers. Forging history is expensive; borrowing it is impossible.
